# Introduction
## Evaluagent API
You can use the EvaluAgent API to access and update information within your EvaluAgent account. The Evaluagent API is organised around [REST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer). REST stands for Representational State Transfer. This is an architectural pattern that describes how distributed systems can expose a consistent interface. When people use the term 'REST API', they are generally referring to an API accessed using the HTTP protocol at a predefined set of URLs.

These URLs represent various resources which can be returned as JSON, HTML or audio files. Often resources have one or more methods that can be performed on them over `HTTP`, like `GET`, `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE`. These actions action represent the verbs Fetch, Create, Update and Delete respectively for those resources. The Evaluagent API is structured using the [JSON:API](https://jsonapi.org/) specification and described using the [OpenAPI](https://www.openapis.org/) specification.

*In order to maintain data sovereignty our API can only be accessed regionally by cluster.*

For customers on our European cluster (**eu-west-1**) the API URL is `api.evaluagent.com`.

For customers on our North America cluster (**us-east**) the API URL is `api.us-east.evaluagent.com`.

For customers on our Australian cluster (**aus**) the API URL is `api.aus.evaluagent.com`.

## Syncing your knowledge base

Context Engine is only as good as the content behind it. The Knowledge Vault endpoints let you sync
documents from wherever they actually live — Confluence, Zendesk Guide, Salesforce Knowledge,
SharePoint — on a schedule, instead of re-uploading files by hand as they change.

Describe what your source currently holds, and let the Vault work out the difference:

1. **Send a manifest.** `PUT /context-engine/knowledge-vault/documents` with `mode=replace`, a
   `source`, and one entry per document — its `external_id`, a `title`, and a SHA-256
   `content_hash` of the text. No file content: this call is a reconciliation, not an upload.
   Start with `dry_run=true`, which writes nothing at all and returns exactly the plan the real
   call would apply.
2. **Read the plan.** It comes back in five buckets. `unchanged` needs nothing. `deleted` has
   already happened. `create` and `update` are yours to action. `skipped` is a removal that was
   refused because the document is attached to a live line item topic — deleting it would leave
   that scorecard with nothing to assess against, so it was left alone and the topics are named
   for a human to detach.
3. **Send the content the plan asked for.** `POST /context-engine/knowledge-vault/documents` for
   each `create`, and `PUT /context-engine/knowledge-vault/documents/{id}/file` for each `update`.
   Pass the same `external_id`, `external_version` and `content_hash` on those calls: that is what
   tells the Vault the document is now in sync, and stops the next manifest asking for it again.
   Replacing a file keeps the document's ID, title, tags and every line item attachment — a naive
   delete-and-reupload would silently unhook your scorecards.
4. **Confirm indexing.** Documents are parsed and embedded asynchronously. Come back and check with
   `filter[indexing_status]=failed` to catch anything that could not be read — a PDF of scanned
   images, for example — rather than assuming a `201` means it is searchable.

Matching is on `external_id`, so renaming a page at the source updates the document you already
have instead of creating a duplicate. And everything is scoped to `source`, so a sync can never
reach documents uploaded by hand, or documents belonging to a different source.

Two things worth building in from the start. Treat `409` on a delete as an expected outcome to
report, not an error to retry, because retrying can never succeed until someone detaches the
document. And prefer `filter[updated_from]` over re-reading everything once your vault is large.

Writes are rate limited to 20 requests per minute per API key, separately from the standard tier,
because each upload costs a file write, a parse and an embedding run. A 500-article knowledge base
still loads in well under an hour.

# QuickStart
Learn how to get started with the Evaluagent API.  This article describes how to quickly get started with the Evaluagent API using `curl` and Basic Authentication.
1. Install `curl` if it isn't already installed on your machine. To check if `curl` is installed, execute `curl --version` in the command line. If the output is information about the version of `curl`, it is installed. If you get a message similar to `command not found: curl`, you need to download and install `curl`. More information can be found [here](https://curl.se/).
2. Create an Evaluagent API key in **Conversations>>Integrations>>API**. Take a note of the **Access Key ID** and **Secret Key**. *Warning: Treat your API key like a password.*
3. Use the `curl` command to make your request. Pass your token in an Authorization header. Replace YOUR-ACCESS-KEY-ID and YOU-SECRET-KEY with your **Access Key ID** and **Secret Key** respectively. `curl –request GET --url "https://YOUR-CLUSTER-REGION/v1/org/users" -u "YOUR-ACCESS-KEY-ID:YOUR-SECRET-KEY"`

# Overview
## API version
Available resources may vary between REST API versions. The current version is `V1`.

## Schema
All API access is over HTTPS and via regional clusters

- Europe: https://api.evaluagent.com.
- North America: https://api.us-east.evaluagent.com.
- Australia: https://api.aus.evaluagent.com.

All data is sent and received as JSON.

Blank fields are included as `null` instead of being omitted.
All timestamps return as a **String** in UTC time, ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`

# Guides
## Using the API
### About the Evaluagent API
When you make a request to the REST API, you will specify an HTTP method and a path. Additionally, you might also specify request headers and path, query, or body parameters. The API will return the response status code, response headers, and potentially a response body. The REST API reference documentation describes the HTTP method, path, and parameters for every operation. It also displays example requests and responses for each operation.

### Making a request
To make a request, first find the HTTP method and the path for the operation that you want to use. For example, the **"List users"** operation uses the `GET` method and the `/org/users` path. Prepend the base URL for the Evaluagent API region (for example: `https://api.evaluagent.com` in Europe) and then the version (currently `v1`) to the path to get the full URL.  For example: `https://api.evaluagent.com/v1/org/users` in Europe.

### Basics of authentication
Evaluagent supports [HTTP Basic authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication).
API keys can be provisioned in the Evaluagent platform under **Conversations>>Integrations>>API**. These are needed to authenticate requests against the API.

You must pass your **Access Key ID** and **Secret Key** in an Authorization header with every request to the API in the format `"Basic YOUR-ACCESS-KEY-ID:YOUR-SECRET-KEY"`, where `YOUR-ACCESS-KEY-ID:YOUR-SECRET-KEY` are Base64 encoded. Many HTTP clients will automatically format in this way for you.

### Bearer Token Authentication
Alternatively, you can use the details above to generate a **Bearer Token**. These expire every 24 hours (+15 minutes) unless they are refreshed, providing a new token and invaliding the existing token. Once a token has been generated, Basic Authentication will be disabled for those credentials. Please note that you must use your Bearer Token when you request to refresh, and this must be done before the current Bearer Token expires. Once a Bearer Token has expired it cannot be used to gain a refreshed token, and Basic Authentication will not be available. After expiration (without refresh), you will need to generate new credentials.

Fetch a list of feedback records — both quality (evaluation) feedback and general
(peer-to-peer) feedback — in a single consistent shape, distinguished by the `type`

quality) are only present for the relevant type. Type-specific filters are ignored when
the other type is requested. Supports pagination; requests default to the first page.

get.description:
Fetch the documents in your Knowledge Vault.

Each document carries its `line_items` — the GenAI line item topics it is attached to — so a
sync job can tell in one request whether a document is safe to delete before attempting it.

Requires the Context Engine feature. Supports pagination and defaults to the first page,
50 per page, most recently updated first.

parameters.name: filter[title]
parameters.description: Partial, case-insensitive match on the document title.

parameters.name: filter[tag_id]
parameters.description: Only documents carrying this tag. Repeatable, or comma-separated; matches any of them.

parameters.name: filter[tag_name]
parameters.description: Only documents carrying this tag name. Repeatable, or comma-separated; matches any of them.

parameters.name: filter[indexing_status]
parameters.description: Restrict to one or more indexing states. Comma-separated.

parameters.name: filter[linked_to_line_items]
parameters.description:
`true` returns only documents attached to at least one line item topic — the ones a delete
will be refused for. `false` returns only unattached documents. Omit the parameter to get
both; passing it empty is rejected rather than read as `false`.

parameters.name: filter[created_from]
parameters.description:
Documents created on or after this point. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD`, taken as the start of that day,
or an ISO 8601 datetime. Both bounds are inclusive. An unreadable value is rejected with 400
rather than silently matching nothing.

parameters.name: filter[created_to]
parameters.description:
Documents created on or before this point. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD`, taken as the **end** of that
day so the whole day is included, or an ISO 8601 datetime, which is honoured exactly. Both
bounds are inclusive.

parameters.name: filter[updated_from]
parameters.description:
Documents updated on or after this point. Same date handling as `created_from`. This is the
filter to use for incremental syncs.

parameters.name: filter[updated_to]
parameters.description: Documents updated on or before this point. Same date handling as `created_to`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order. Prefix with `-` for descending. Options: `title`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Defaults to `-updated_at`.

parameters.name: page[number]
parameters.description: When paginated, the page number to request. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: filter[sync_state]
parameters.description:
One or more sync states, comma-separated: `synced`, `stale`, `failed`,
`removed_at_source`, `orphaned`. The counterpart of `filter[indexing_status]` — this is
how you find the documents a source has moved on from, removed, or that someone has edited
locally, without paging the whole Vault.

An unrecognised state is rejected with `400` rather than returning an empty set, because a
filter you act on should not answer a typo with "none". Each value in the list is checked,
so `stale,removed_at_source` is accepted and `stale,stail` is refused whole.

parameters.name: filter[connection]
parameters.description:
One or more connection ids, comma-separated — the documents belonging to those sources.

`none` selects the documents that belong to no source: the hand-uploaded ones, which a sync
must never touch and which cannot be named with an id. It **combines** with ids rather than
replacing them, so `none,<id>` returns the hand-uploaded documents *and* that source's.

A value that is neither `none` nor a well-formed id is rejected with `400`. A well-formed
id that names nothing — including one belonging to another account — is not an error: it
simply matches no documents.

parameters.name: page[size]
parameters.description: Documents per page. Defaults to 50, maximum 250.

200.description: Returns an array of Knowledge Vault documents

400.description:
An unrecognised `filter` key, or an unreadable date. Both are rejected rather than ignored,
so a typo cannot silently widen or empty the result set that a sync job then acts on.

post.description:
Upload a single document to the Knowledge Vault as `multipart/form-data`.

Accepted formats are PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, CSV and HTML (`.html` or `.htm`), up to 10 MB per
file, and the file must not be empty. Titles must be
unique within the account.

To attach the document to a source — closing the loop on a `create` from
`PUT /documents` — pass `connection` and `external_id` together, optionally with
`external_version`, `external_url` and `content_hash`. Omit them for an ordinary upload and
nothing changes.

The document is queued for parsing and embedding on success, so the response returns
`indexing_status: pending`. Poll the document, or list with
`filter[indexing_status]=failed`, to confirm it became searchable.

**Rate limited to 20 requests per minute** per API key, separately from the standard tier,
because each upload costs a file write, a parse and an embedding run.

file.description: The document itself. PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, CSV or HTML (`.html` or `.htm`), maximum 10 MB, and not empty.

title.description: The document's name in the Knowledge Vault. Must be unique within the account.

tags.description:
Tag IDs or names. A name that does not already exist is created; a name that does
exist resolves to the existing tag rather than duplicating it, matched
case-insensitively. A value in UUID form is always read as an ID: if no tag in your
account has it the request is rejected, rather than a tag being created under the
ID as its name.

connection.description:
The source this document belongs to, from the `connection.id` returned by
`PUT /documents`. Must be sent together with `external_id`; sending one without
the other is refused (`incomplete_sync_identity`), because a document
half-attached to a source is invisible to the sync that created it.

external_url.description: Deep link back to the document at the source.

external_version.description: Your version identifier for the content being uploaded.

content_hash.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the text you extracted. Recording it here is what marks the document
in sync — without it the next manifest asks for the same content again.

400.description:
Validation failed - a missing or empty file, a missing title, or an unknown tag ID.
Field-level detail is under `meta.validation`.

409.description:
Either a document with this title already exists (`duplicate_document_title`), or the
connection already holds a document for this `external_id` (`duplicate_external_id`) — one
source item is one document, so replace its file rather than creating a second.

Nothing is stored in either case: the row is rolled back and the uploaded file discarded.

415.description: The file format is not supported (`unsupported_file_format`). The message names the accepted formats.

put.description:
Reconcile one source's documents against a manifest of its desired end state, and get back a
plan of what changed.

**The manifest carries no file content, by design.** A request body is capped well below the
size of a real knowledge base, and a multipart request has an undocumented ceiling on how many
files it may carry — one it enforces by silently discarding the rest. So this endpoint takes
ids and content hashes, works out what needs to happen, and applies the half it can:
reconciling metadata, and removing what the source no longer has. Content for the `create` and
`update` buckets is then sent through `POST /documents` and `PUT /documents/{id}/file`, which
already validate formats and enforce the size limit.

That split is what makes the endpoint safe to point at a live account. The destructive half —
the part where a mistake costs you documents — is centralised here, behind `dry_run`.

**Everything is scoped to `source`.** "Documents not in the manifest are deleted" applies only
to documents belonging to that source. Documents uploaded by hand, and documents belonging to
another source, are never touched.

**Matching is on `external_id`, never the title.** A page renamed at the source updates the
document it already has, rather than creating a second one beside it.

Always returns `207`, because the answer is per item: a manifest can legitimately create some
documents, leave others alone, and be blocked on one.

207.description:
The plan, applied unless `dry_run` was set. Check `meta.requires_follow_up` to see whether
anything is left for you to do.

400.description: The manifest failed validation. `meta.validation` carries the field-level detail.

409.description:
A connection with that name already exists with a different `source.type`
(`connection_source_type_mismatch`). Refused rather than re-pointed, because re-typing a
connection would make every document under it look missing on the next sync.

422.description:
Two entries share an `external_id` (`duplicate_external_id`), so the manifest describes the
same source item twice and there is no safe way to choose between them. Also returned when
`external_id` is sent as a JSON number rather than a string.

- For conversations that include a recorded audio file you will need to first use the `/quality/imported-contacts/upload-audio` endpoint to upload that audio file.  Then using the returned `path` reference use this endpoint to import the related metadata for your conversation.

Conversation `responses` are processed asynchronously after the request returns: a successful response confirms the contact was created and its responses accepted for processing, and the responses will typically be visible on the contact shortly afterwards. A `GET` for the contact immediately after import may briefly return it without its responses.

Use this endpoint to correct or add custom metadata fields on a conversation you have already imported, without re-importing it. The conversation is identified by the `reference` it was imported under.

Only metadata is changed. To change any other attribute of the conversation, or to add responses, re-import it.

**Fields you send are merged into the conversation's existing metadata.**
- A field you send with a value replaces that field, or creates it if the conversation did not have it.
- A field you send as `null` is **removed** from the conversation.
- A field you do not send is left exactly as it was.

Newly created fields become available as reporting and conversation filters automatically. Updated values are reflected in conversation filtering immediately, and in Conversation Insights reporting once the conversation has been re-aggregated.

Values are stored with the JSON type you send them as. Sending `"22"` where the field previously held `22` will store the field as text, which excludes it from numeric filters — send numbers as numbers.

Some field names are reserved by Evaluagent and are rejected. These are names we write or read ourselves — the audio and video pointers (`audio_url`, `video_url`, `sample_rate`), the external link (`external_url`, `conversation_url`, `linkToThirdParty`), transcription and analytics fields (`transcription_provider`, `totalWords`), fields mirroring a column (`channel_name`, `handling_time`), and any name beginning with `__`. Field names cannot contain a full stop, and `metadata` must be an object of named fields rather than a list.

If two requests update the same conversation at the same time, changes to different fields are both kept; if both change the same field, the last one to complete wins.

**Please note there is rate-limiting in place for this endpoint. Maximum 100 requests per-minute, based on API credentials.**

Progress of the document through parsing and embedding. `pending` immediately after upload
or a file replacement, `complete` once the document is searchable by Context Engine, and
`failed` if it could not be parsed (for example a PDF containing only scanned images).

line_items.description:
The GenAI line item topics this document is attached to. Attaching and detaching is done in
the application, not through this API — the field is read-only here. An empty array means
the document is safe to delete; anything else means `DELETE` will be refused with a 409.

source.description:
Where this document came from, or `null` where a person uploaded it. Null is a meaningful
answer, not a missing one: it tells a sync job the document is not its to manage, and it is
what keeps `mode=replace` away from documents added by hand.

content_hash.description: The hash of the text currently stored — not the hash the source last reported.

sync_state.description:
Where the document stands relative to its source. Deliberately separate from
`indexing_status`: the two answer different questions and can disagree in every
combination. `stale` means the source has moved on and the new content has not arrived.
`removed_at_source` means the source no longer has it and a person needs to decide.
`orphaned` means it was edited here after being synced, so neither copy is authoritative
and a sync will not overwrite it.

mode.description:
Only `replace` is supported. Required rather than defaulted, because a `PUT` to this path
deletes the documents it does not mention.

dry_run.description:
Return the plan without applying any of it. Nothing is written — not the documents, not even
the connection itself, if it does not exist yet.

on_missing.description:
What to do with a document this source holds that the manifest does not mention.
`delete` removes it. `archive` keeps it and sets `sync_state` to `removed_at_source`, which is
the safer choice for an unattended job: a source that briefly returns a short manifest cannot
then empty your Vault.

source.description:
The source this manifest describes. Resolved by `name` within your account, and created on
first use — there is no separate call to make. Everything this endpoint reconciles is scoped
to it, so a sync can never touch documents uploaded by hand or belonging to another source.

type.description: Your identifier for the kind of system this is. Free-form.

name.description:
Names the connection. Matched case-insensitively. Reusing a name with a different `type`
is refused, because it would silently repoint a whole document set at another system.

external_account_id.description: The site, tenant or subdomain at the far end. Followed if it changes.

documents.description:
The desired end state for this source. An empty array is valid and means the source now holds
nothing — the most destructive request this endpoint accepts, and the reason `dry_run` exists.

Note that no file content is carried here. See the endpoint description.

external_id.description:
The document's stable id in your system. This, not the title, is what matches a manifest
entry to a Vault document — so renaming a page at the source updates it in place instead
of creating a duplicate.

title.description:
The title to give the document. Applied on create, and followed on rename. Titles are
unique per account, so a rename into one that is taken is reported in `warnings` and the
existing title is kept.

content_hash.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the document's text as you extracted it. This decides whether the document
needs re-uploading — not the version — so a version bump that does not change the text
costs nothing.

external_version.description: Your version identifier. Recorded, and reported back on change, but not used for matching.

tags.description:
Tag names, created if they do not exist. Applied additively: tags added by hand in the
app are never removed by a sync.

code.description:

SyncPlan.description:
What the sync did, or — under `dry_run` — what it would do. Every manifest entry and every
document this source already held appears in exactly one bucket.

create.description: In the manifest, not in the Vault. Upload the content with `POST /documents`.

update.description:
Matched, but the content hash moved. Send the new file with `PUT /documents/{id}/file`.
Until you do, the document's `sync_state` is `stale` and it keeps serving its previous text.

unchanged.description: Matched, and the hash agrees. Metadata was reconciled; nothing was re-indexed.

deleted.description: Held by this source, absent from the manifest.

applied.description:
Whether this removal actually happened. Always true on a completed run. After an
interrupted one (`meta.aborted`), it is the only way to tell what was destroyed from what
was merely planned.

skipped.description:
Would have been removed, but is attached to a live GenAI line item topic. It was left intact
and the blocking topics are named — a sync never strips grounding out of a scorecard in use.
Detach it in the app, or re-run with `on_missing=archive`.

SyncWarning.description:
Applied, but not entirely as asked. Distinct from `skipped`, which is work that did not happen at
all — a warning means the document is in sync and one attribute of it is not.

id.description: Null for a warning about a manifest entry that has no document yet.

code.description:
`title_conflict` — the source renamed a document into a title already in use, so it kept its
previous one. `title_unavailable` — a `create` whose title is already taken, so the upload
that would follow will be refused. Titles are unique per account.

responses.description:
An array of responses/messages.

**Speaker Identification Priority:**
- If both `speaker_id` and `speaker_email` are provided, `speaker_id` takes precedence
- At least one of `speaker_id` or `speaker_email` must be provided

**Speaker Type Flags - Mutual Exclusivity Rules:**
- `speaker_is_customer`, `speaker_is_bot`, and `speaker_is_system` are mutually exclusive - only one should be true per response
- If `speaker_is_customer` is true, neither `speaker_is_bot`, `speaker_is_system`, nor `internal_note` can be true
- When none of these flags are true, the speaker is assumed to be an agent/human representative
- `internal_note` is independent of bot/system flags but cannot be true when `speaker_is_customer` is true

**Default Behaviour:**
- All boolean flags default to `false` if not provided
- A response with no speaker type flags set is treated as an agent message

Indicates the speaker is a bot/automated system (e.g., chatbot, auto-responder).
Mutually exclusive with `speaker_is_customer` and `speaker_is_system`.

Defaults to false.

Indicates this is an internal note not visible to customers (e.g., agent-to-agent communication).
Cannot be true when `speaker_is_customer` is true. Can be combined with `speaker_is_bot` or `speaker_is_system`.
Defaults to false.

agent_email.description: The EvaluAgent email address of the agent. Either an `agent_id` or `agent_email` must be present in all requests. `agent_id` will be used if both are provided. The agent must be assigned to a `Contract` and a `Group`.

channel.description: The name of the channel which must match an existing channel within your system

assigned_at.description: Time when the contact was assigned to the user

solved_at.description: Time when the contact was solved by the user

handling_time.description: Handling time of the imported contact in seconds

audio_file_path.description: Path to an audio file returned from the **Upload audio** endpoint.

metadata.description: An object of optional custom metadata fields

responses.description:
An array of responses/messages.

**Speaker Identification Priority:**
- If both `speaker_id` and `speaker_email` are provided, `speaker_id` takes precedence
- At least one of `speaker_id` or `speaker_email` must be provided

**Speaker Type Flags - Mutual Exclusivity Rules:**
- `speaker_is_customer`, `speaker_is_bot`, and `speaker_is_system` are mutually exclusive - only one should be true per response
- If `speaker_is_customer` is true, neither `speaker_is_bot`, `speaker_is_system`, nor `internal_note` can be true
- When none of these flags are true, the speaker is assumed to be an agent/human representative
- `internal_note` is independent of bot/system flags but cannot be true when `speaker_is_customer` is true

**Default Behaviour:**
- All boolean flags default to `false` if not provided
- A response with no speaker type flags set is treated as an agent message

speaker_id.description: The EvaluAgent user UUID of the speaker. Either a `speaker_id` or `speaker_email` must be present in all responses. `speaker_id` will be used if both are provided.

speaker_email.description: The email address of the speaker. Either a `speaker_id` or `speaker_email` must be present in all responses. `speaker_id` will be used if both are provided.

response_id.description: A unique identifier for this response

message.example: Hi, I’ve been trying to resolve an issue regarding my online account.

speaker_is_customer.description:
Indicates the speaker is a customer. Mutually exclusive with `speaker_is_bot` and `speaker_is_system`.
When true, `internal_note` cannot be true.
Defaults to false.

speaker_is_bot.description:
Indicates the speaker is a bot/automated system (e.g., chatbot, auto-responder).
Mutually exclusive with `speaker_is_customer` and `speaker_is_system`.
Defaults to false.

speaker_is_system.description:
Indicates a system-generated message (e.g., "ticket closed", "agent assigned", status changes).
Mutually exclusive with `speaker_is_customer` and `speaker_is_bot`.
Defaults to false.

internal_note.description:
Indicates this is an internal note not visible to customers (e.g., agent-to-agent communication).
Cannot be true when `speaker_is_customer` is true. Can be combined with `speaker_is_bot` or `speaker_is_system`.
Defaults to false.

reference.description: The reference the conversation was imported under. Must match an existing imported conversation on your contract.

metadata.description:
An object of the custom metadata fields to change. At least one field is required.

Send a value to set or replace a field, or `null` to remove it. Fields you do not send are left unchanged.
The complete metadata of the conversation after your changes were merged in. Includes fields you did not send.

LineItemReference.description: A GenAI line item topic the document is attached to.

title.description: The document's name within the Knowledge Vault. Unique per account, and what the UI shows in the File Name column.

description.example: How to handle an inbound complaint

file_name.description:
The name of the file as uploaded. `null` for documents uploaded before this field was
recorded — use `title` to identify a document, not this.

file_size.description: Size of the stored file in bytes.

indexing_status.description:
Progress of the document through parsing and embedding. `pending` immediately after upload
or a file replacement, `complete` once the document is searchable by Context Engine, and
`failed` if it could not be parsed (for example a PDF containing only scanned images).

line_items.description:
The GenAI line item topics this document is attached to. Attaching and detaching is done in
the application, not through this API — the field is read-only here. An empty array means
the document is safe to delete; anything else means `DELETE` will be refused with a 409.

source.description:
Where this document came from, or `null` where a person uploaded it. Null is a meaningful
answer, not a missing one: it tells a sync job the document is not its to manage, and it is
what keeps `mode=replace` away from documents added by hand.

content_hash.description: The hash of the text currently stored — not the hash the source last reported.

sync_state.description:
Where the document stands relative to its source. Deliberately separate from
`indexing_status`: the two answer different questions and can disagree in every
combination. `stale` means the source has moved on and the new content has not arrived.
`removed_at_source` means the source no longer has it and a person needs to decide.
`orphaned` means it was edited here after being synced, so neither copy is authoritative
and a sync will not overwrite it.

document_count.description: How many documents currently carry this tag.

line_items.description:
The line item topics reachable through this tag's documents, matching the Line Items column
on the Tags table. Informational only: a tag is never itself attached to a line item, and
deleting a tag never detaches a document from one.

ids.description: Document IDs to delete. Maximum 200 per request.

status.description:
Per-document outcome. `204` deleted, `409` refused because the document is attached to a
line item topic, `404` no such document in this account.

error.description: Present only when `status` is not 204. Same shape as a top-level error object.

action.description: Whether to add the tags to, or remove them from, the given documents.

document_ids.description: Documents to change. Maximum 200 per request.

tags.description:
Tag IDs or names. On `apply`, a name that does not exist is created. On `remove`, only existing
tags are matched — a name that does not exist is a no-op, never a new tag.

title.description: Must be unique within the account.

tags.description:
Replaces the document's entire tag set. Omit the field to leave tags untouched; pass an empty
array to clear them. Names that do not exist are created.

code.description:
`document_linked_to_line_item` when a document is attached to a line item topic,
`duplicate_document_title` when the title is already used, `duplicate_tag_name` when the
tag name is already used.

detail.example: This document cannot be deleted because it is attached to one or more line item topics. Remove the attachment before deleting.

mode.description:
Only `replace` is supported. Required rather than defaulted, because a `PUT` to this path
deletes the documents it does not mention.

dry_run.description:
Return the plan without applying any of it. Nothing is written — not the documents, not even
the connection itself, if it does not exist yet.

on_missing.description:
What to do with a document this source holds that the manifest does not mention.
`delete` removes it. `archive` keeps it and sets `sync_state` to `removed_at_source`, which is
the safer choice for an unattended job: a source that briefly returns a short manifest cannot
then empty your Vault.

source.description:
The source this manifest describes. Resolved by `name` within your account, and created on
first use — there is no separate call to make. Everything this endpoint reconciles is scoped
to it, so a sync can never touch documents uploaded by hand or belonging to another source.

type.description: Your identifier for the kind of system this is. Free-form.

name.description:
Names the connection. Matched case-insensitively. Reusing a name with a different `type`
is refused, because it would silently repoint a whole document set at another system.

external_account_id.description: The site, tenant or subdomain at the far end. Followed if it changes.

documents.description:
The desired end state for this source. An empty array is valid and means the source now holds
nothing — the most destructive request this endpoint accepts, and the reason `dry_run` exists.

Note that no file content is carried here. See the endpoint description.

external_id.description:
The document's stable id in your system. This, not the title, is what matches a manifest
entry to a Vault document — so renaming a page at the source updates it in place instead
of creating a duplicate.

title.description:
The title to give the document. Applied on create, and followed on rename. Titles are
unique per account, so a rename into one that is taken is reported in `warnings` and the
existing title is kept.

content_hash.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the document's text as you extracted it. This decides whether the document
needs re-uploading — not the version — so a version bump that does not change the text
costs nothing.

external_version.description: Your version identifier. Recorded, and reported back on change, but not used for matching.

tags.description:
Tag names, created if they do not exist. Applied additively: tags added by hand in the
app are never removed by a sync.

SyncPlan.description:
What the sync did, or — under `dry_run` — what it would do. Every manifest entry and every
document this source already held appears in exactly one bucket.

create.description: In the manifest, not in the Vault. Upload the content with `POST /documents`.

update.description:
Matched, but the content hash moved. Send the new file with `PUT /documents/{id}/file`.
Until you do, the document's `sync_state` is `stale` and it keeps serving its previous text.

unchanged.description: Matched, and the hash agrees. Metadata was reconciled; nothing was re-indexed.

deleted.description: Held by this source, absent from the manifest.

applied.description:
Whether this removal actually happened. Always true on a completed run. After an
interrupted one (`meta.aborted`), it is the only way to tell what was destroyed from what
was merely planned.

skipped.description:
Would have been removed, but is attached to a live GenAI line item topic. It was left intact
and the blocking topics are named — a sync never strips grounding out of a scorecard in use.
Detach it in the app, or re-run with `on_missing=archive`.

SyncWarning.description:
Applied, but not entirely as asked. Distinct from `skipped`, which is work that did not happen at
all — a warning means the document is in sync and one attribute of it is not.

id.description: Null for a warning about a manifest entry that has no document yet.

code.description:
`title_conflict` — the source renamed a document into a title already in use, so it kept its
previous one. `title_unavailable` — a `create` whose title is already taken, so the upload
that would follow will be refused. Titles are unique per account.

detail.example: The source renamed this document to "Refunds policy", but that title is already in use. It kept the title "Ops / Refunds".

id.description:
Null under `dry_run` where the source does not exist yet — nothing was created, so
there is no id to hand back. Check `exists` rather than testing for null.

exists.description: Whether this connection is stored. False only on a `dry_run` for a source that has never synced.

error.description:
Present only when the run stopped part-way. The plan is still returned, with `applied` on
each removal saying what actually happened — re-running is safe, because the next plan is
recomputed from what is really stored.

requires_follow_up.description: True when anything needs the caller to act — content to send, or a conflict to resolve.

aborted.description:
True when the run stopped part-way. The plan then describes intent, and `applied` on each
removal describes outcome.
